clue.text: Joanne getting pregnant? Me too!

parts.note: Jo is the short form of the name Joanne
'in the club' is British slang for pregnant (from 'in the pudding club')

explanation.surface: A friend announces that Joanne is expecting, and someone chimes in that they are too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the club' is informal British slang for being pregnant, so Joanne getting pregnant is JO in the club.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said to someone describing a misfortune or situation the speaker shares, much like saying 'same here'.

clue.text: Fragmented images in shark film inspiring disgust, occasionally

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the film takes the other letters into itself

parts.note: Jaws is Spielberg's 1975 film about a great white shark

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of disgust is used

explanation.surface: A shark movie supposedly cut into broken pictures that occasionally provoke revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shark film' is the 1975 Spielberg thriller, and 'inspiring' is read literally as breathing in, taking the picked letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Jigsaw puzzles are pictures cut into interlocking pieces, so they are images broken into fragments.

clue.text: Inuits moving around on site

indicators.note: the letters of Inuits are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: Inuit people travelling about a location they are working on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in the original place, which is to say right there at the location.

clue.text: Written record of time on sprint race almost changed

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' places the first piece above, so before, the rest
changed means the letters of sprint and the shortened race are rearranged
almost means the word race loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A timed record of a sprint race that was nearly altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims race to RAC; 'changed' shuffles SPRINT with RAC, and T for time sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A transcript is a written copy of what was said, such as court proceedings.

clue.text: Work in a school, but not tons, for a head

indicators.note: 'but not' tells us to leave the following letter out

parts.note: to teach is to work in a school

explanation.surface: Someone works at a school, though not in a heavy-duty role, for a headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a head' sounds like a headteacher in the school picture; it means per person.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices given per person, so much a head, are prices for every individual one.

clue.text: Letter from two lads around New Year

indicators.note: around here means the letters are turned about into a different arrangement

parts.note: two copies of the word lad

explanation.surface: A letter arriving from two young men at about New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like a written message but means someone who lets out property.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlady rents out rooms or a house, so she is one who lets: a crossword-only sense.

clue.text: Great country music composer named Benjamin on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than read, signalling a word that sounds alike

parts.note: Benjamin Britten was the English composer of Peter Grimes

explanation.surface: A great nation's music, its composer Benjamin being played on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Britain is the island nation of England, Scotland and Wales, so it is the 'Great' country.

clue.text: Summer month with American in state capital

parts.note: August is a month of the northern summer

explanation.surface: Spending a summer month with an American in some state's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Augusta is the capital of the US state of Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is the seat of government of Maine, one of the United States.

clue.text: Macron, drunk around one, promises to pay for bitter

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters wrap about the next piece
drunk means the letters of Macron are reeling into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: French President Macron, tipsy, signs IOUs for a pint of bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' looks like the beer in the surface; it is the definition, meaning resentful.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimonious describes angry, resentful exchanges, so it is a synonym of bitter.

clue.text: Orphan girl in musical, dressed by king, is smarter

indicators.note: dressed by means wrapped in, so the king's letters go round the girl

parts.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, King Charles
Annie is the orphan heroine of the musical Annie

explanation.surface: The little orphan of the musical, costumed by a king, looks smarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smarter' suggests better dressed in the surface; here it means shrewder.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd, so cannier is the comparative meaning more astute.

clue.text: Breed butterfly for naval officer

parts.note: to rear animals is to breed them
the red admiral is a butterfly; admiral alone names the type

explanation.surface: An instruction to breed a type of butterfly, for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear admiral is a senior commissioned rank in the navy, below vice admiral.

clue.text: Admitting nothing, criminal started trial

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the shuffled letters take the next piece inside
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of started are bent into a new order

parts.note: O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A criminal pleaded not guilty, admitting nothing, and his trial began.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom picture makes 'trial' look legal; it is a test drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A road test is a trial of a vehicle driven on public roads to check how it performs.

clue.text: Woolly beast in mountain area by Canada's borders

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: borders means the outside letters, the first and last

parts.note: the word Canada, the possessive just linking it to its borders

explanation.surface: A shaggy animal found in high country beside Canada's frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American camelid kept for its fine fleece, so it is a wool-bearing animal.

clue.text: Dangerous mutt in Essex keeps being dirty

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A dangerous dog in Essex keeps getting filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is an English county east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Smuttiness is the state of being obscene or grimy, the noun for being smutty.

clue.text: Room where servicemen eat pickle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a military dining hall
second meaning: a pickle is a predicament or muddle

explanation.surface: A canteen where soldiers have pickles with their meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the forces' dining room and a state of confusion or difficulty.

clue.text: Public relations by current "Queen of Pop", a diva

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
Madonna is known as the Queen of Pop

explanation.surface: A publicist managing the latest Queen of Pop, who is quite the diva.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna is the leading female opera singer, and by extension a temperamental star.

clue.text: Where to see stallions run into awful mud fast

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the other letters
awful suggests a mess, so mud and fast are jumbled together

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Horses gallop quickly into horrible mud.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud farm is where stallions are kept for breeding horses.

clue.text: Stop things going crazy in evening entertainment venues

indicators.note: going crazy means the letters of stop and things run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: An appeal to stop things getting out of hand at late-night entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightspots are clubs and bars open at night, places people go out to in the evening.

clue.text: Flabbergast Richard, catching kind of flu

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: Astonish Richard by catching some strain of influenza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' looks like catching the flu; it is the signal that the answer is held in the text.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric flu is the everyday name for a stomach bug, a type of 'flu' affecting the gut.

clue.text: The sound of a hit 1980s pop group

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a noise of a forceful blow
second meaning: ...! was the George Michael duo of the 1980s

explanation.surface: The sound of a chart hit by an eighties band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' suggests a chart record; one meaning is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an onomatopoeic noise of an impact, and also the name of a 1980s duo.

clue.text: Explain to me why house contains old toilet

indicators.note: contains means the house holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a home is a house
WC is water closet, a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone demands to know why their house still has an antique lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal question 'how come?' asks for a reason, meaning why is it so.

clue.text: Lofty Scottish mountain is a capital attraction

parts.note: lofty means tall, big
ben is the Scots word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A tall Highland peak is a top tourist draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' sounds like 'excellent'; here it means London, where the great clock bell hangs.
explanation.definitionFit: The great bell in the Elizabeth Tower in Westminster is a famous London tourist sight.

clue.text: Dealing with team correctly positioned on pitch

parts.note: on means about or concerning, dealing with a topic
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Handling a squad that is arranged properly on the field.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a player is onside when legally placed, not offside, on the playing field.

clue.text: Defeat for Charles I, showing courtesy with a Republican

parts.note: civil means polite, showing courtesy

explanation.surface: King Charles I loses, yet is polite to a republican opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles I lost the English Civil War to Parliament and was executed in 1649.
explanation.definitionFit: The English conflict of the 1640s ended with the King's defeat, so the war is his loss.

clue.text: Love for tennis from Alcaraz, McEnroe and Becker too, in the end

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Tennis stars Alcaraz, McEnroe and Becker all eventually loving the game.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring 'love' means a score of nothing, the number nought.

clue.text: Top expert follows what people browsing the internet do

indicators.note: follows means the expert's word comes after the other

parts.words: what people browsing the internet do
parts.note: people who browse the internet surf the web
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A skilled user copies what web browsers do.
explanation.definitionFit: The surface of something is its upper face or top layer.

clue.text: Involve brother, cutting linden tree back

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the brother goes inside
back means the tree's name is read from right to left

parts.note: the lime is also called the linden

explanation.surface: Get a brother involved in felling the linden tree out the back.
explanation.walkthrough: Linden is another name for the lime tree, not the citrus fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to drag them into a dispute or difficulty, so to involve them.

clue.text: People in parliament's lower chamber unusually seen showing nous

parts.note: the Commons is the elected lower house of the UK Parliament

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of seen appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: MPs in the lower house, for once, are seen being sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Commons is the lower chamber of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is British informal for practical good sense, the sound judgement ordinary people share.
